records.claimSummary: The note maps the invoice path of the Ledgerline billing service (commit a41c9e2).
records.conditionSummary: Refunds, dunning and the customer portal are out of scope.
records.mustConvey: refunds, dunning and the customer portal are not covered
records.bindingReason: The map still covers the invoice path without the exclusion; the exclusion is a scope note that must appear somewhere.
records.notes: Frame g9 takeaway mentions invoice path, commit and manual review but not the exclusions. Arrows only join ax-n pairs (ax1->n1, ax4->n4).

records.claimSummary: collectUsage selects the account's usage_events rows inside the period and groups them by meter into usage lines.
records.bindingReason: Read alone, the selection sentence implies every in-period event is counted, which is false for is_test events.
records.notes: u2_n2/u1_n6 describe collecting usage at module/step level without claiming all events; not counted as claim cards.

records.claimSummary: priceUsage (probably) also reads the discounts table.
records.conditionSummary: No call site for discountFor found; the link is unconfirmed until traced.
records.mustConvey: the discounts read is unconfirmed / only probable (no call site found)
records.bindingReason: Stating that priceUsage reads discounts without the hedge presents an unverified link as fact, which may be false.

records.claimSummary: TaxClient.quote sends the draft invoice to Taxwell over HTTPS.
records.conditionSummary: The request times out after 8 seconds.
records.bindingReason: The quote call still sends the draft to Taxwell; the timeout bounds it but does not falsify the sentence.
records.notes: Frame g4 takeaway says the integration 'lacks documented ... timeout handling', which does not convey the 8 s value (and arguably blurs it with the unknown timeout outcome).

records.claimSummary: generateInvoice calls TaxClient.quote to get tax from Taxwell for the draft.
records.conditionSummary: Retry behaviour is undocumented: quote has no retry code, and caller/library retries and the invoice's fate on timeout are unknown.
records.mustConvey: tax provider retry behaviour / timeout outcome is unknown; quote has no retry code
records.bindingReason: The call sequence remains true; the unknown retry behaviour is a reliability caveat that must be somewhere in the notes.
records.notes: u1_n10 sits in g0, whose takeaway is silent; the g0->g4 arrow joins frames, not the card.

records.claimSummary: After the commit, generateInvoice publishes invoice.finalized to billing-events.
records.conditionSummary: If publishing fails after commit, the code logs and returns, so an invoice can exist without its event; no re-send job found.
records.mustConvey: publish failure after commit leaves an invoice without its event (logged only, no re-send)
records.bindingReason: The claim implies every finalized invoice gets an invoice.finalized event, which is false when publishing fails after commit.
records.notes: g5 takeaway 'event publishing failures after commit are not handled' judged recognisable. Binding could be argued as set since the code does call publish; chose claim because the summary/flow cards imply guaranteed delivery.

records.claimSummary: InvoiceDraft has fields accountId, period, lines, subtotalCents and optional taxCents.
records.conditionSummary: taxCents stays undefined until TaxClient.quote returns.
records.mustConvey: taxCents is undefined until the tax quote returns
records.bindingReason: The interface (with taxCents optional) is accurate without the note; the timing is an added detail.
records.notes: g6 takeaway says 'taxCents conditionally populated' but not the condition (until quote returns), so not counted as carrier.

records.claimSummary: billing/pricing acts as the pricing boundary; a pricing change should only need edits there.
records.conditionSummary: This is an interpretation, not a rule the code enforces; nothing stops another module querying price_plans.
records.mustConvey: interpretation only / not enforced; other modules could query price_plans directly
records.bindingReason: Stated as fact, the boundary claim becomes misleading as soon as any module queries price_plans directly, which nothing prevents.
records.notes: u8_n1 hedges ('appears', 'seems') which partially conveys interpretation, but the not-enforced part sits in u8_n2 via a 'caveat' arrow. Frame g7 states the boundary flatly; it contains u8_n2 but containment is not an arrow, so labelled separated (low-medium certainty on how frames-as-claim-cards should be treated).

notes: No records for: module list and fixed call order (u5-u19, plain facts), u26 integer cents (a claim, not a limit), u37 rollback (carried by 'single transaction' wording in u6_n1/u6_n2 and judged an elaboration), u38/u41/u47 'I found no / did not read' epistemic hedges (minor; the cards keep them), open questions u52-u55 (questions, not conditions), and u57 (duplicates r3 and r5). The summary caveat u57 is covered through r3/r5 carriers.
